diagnosis: Live PnL fell 9.9 and replay lost 12.1, including 11.4 in the second half. Replay ended flat in every stock, peaked at two gross lots and used at most 13 requests/s. The clearest problem is which fills the bot accepts, not insufficient request capacity. AVGO accounted for 72% of the replay loss on 16% of fills. Its average adverse markout was nearly as large at 1s as at 5s, so waiting for the six-observation, 5s breaker cannot protect the first bad fill. There is a specific pre-fill decision worth testing: when no wall qualifies at the planned entry price, the touch-probe branch can raise a bid or lower an ask by up to one tick beyond the unrounded price the risk model approved. A qualifying two-way touch shows activity; it does not establish that surrendering that tick is profitable. The one-tick concession cannot itself explain an eleven-tick markout. It can, however, admit a fill the model priced too cheaply to take. The supplied aggregates do not establish whether either stopped AVGO position opened through this branch.
strategy_plan: Run one AVGO-only comparison: keep a wallless one-lot probe at the touch only if its actual resting price preserves the plan's half-spread from reservation value. Otherwise set funded volume to zero; do not post a deeper order in its place. Keep the touch price visible to the existing shadow round-trip screen, keep wall-backed entries and inventory-reducing exits unchanged, and leave the other seven names alone. AVGO is the pilot because its large moves showed continuation in both C4 (+1.64 ticks) and C5 (+2.70 ticks), not because the latest window proves every AVGO quote is bad. This is a candidate, not a verified promotion. Run `python3 -m unittest tests/test_bot.py`, then `python3 bot/backtest.py /home/workspace/data/autoloop_28_073055/snapshots/cycle_005 --strategy runner:BacktestBot` against the −12.1 Champion. Match changed opening orders to their completed round trips: count profitable trips forfeited as well as losses avoided. Reject a no-op, a disconnect, or an improvement attributable only to ending inventory. Check the two Nacht chunks and the next untouched chunk before generalizing or sizing up.
insights: AVGO's replay markout worsened by only 0.82 ticks between 1s and 5s, versus 10.56 adverse ticks already present at 1s. For this name, inspect the opening quote before tuning the 5s breaker.
CRWV generated 56% of replay fills but only 0.3 of the 12.1 loss. A broad reduction in fill count is a poor success metric; compare PnL on the specific completed round trips a price rule changes.
